what_happened: The job was to find and remove the cause of the longer checks stage (the ratio rose from about 0.2 to 0.6). The verifier rejected it at the final verdict. One of 5 acceptance criteria was unmet: a note must state the cause, cite the specific crates/ code path, and give evidence (measured or labeled estimate). No failed checks are listed. There were two major findings and no blocker. (1) The note's stated cause does not explain the rise from 0.2 to 0.6, because the jobs it cites as evidence were already in the window that gave 0.2. (2) The note guessed at the cause where the job records could have been read. It also missed the largest local checks cost in the window: full-suite `cargo test --locked` demonstrations, which cost 13 to 15 minutes each (crates/athena-core/src/run/checks.rs demonstration_runs).
cause: The job is a diagnose-then-fix task, but nothing requires the diagnosis to be backed by data before it is accepted. The criterion asked only that a note name a cause with "measured or labeled estimate" evidence. That lets a guess pass as a labeled estimate, and no step checks that the cause explains the change in the metric. Athena has per-stage timing records for past jobs, but the producer is not required to compare the before and after windows, or to rank the stage's cost components, such as demonstration runs against ordinary checks. A cause that fits only the cited jobs, which were already in the baseline window, is caught only when the verifier reads the note. The same pattern of fixing or explaining the symptom without a diagnosed root cause has already been rejected on the page-output jobs.
prevention: For bug or regression jobs, make the diagnosis a required, checked result. The accepted reading should require a root-cause section that has three parts. First, a table of the metric by window (before and after) built from the recorded stage timings. Second, a ranked breakdown of the stage's cost components, with the share each one takes. Third, a statement of which component changed between the windows. Athena should check mechanically that every job cited as evidence falls inside the "after" window and outside the "before" window. A cause that has no such data should be refused as unevidenced. A fix step should come only after this note passes.
proposed_request: Find the cause of the rise in the checks stage share of job time (about 0.2 to about 0.6) and remove it. Do this in two parts in one job. Part 1 is a note in docs/design/checks-stage-slowdown.md. Read the recorded per-stage timings of past jobs and split them into a before window (ratio about 0.2) and an after window (ratio about 0.6). List the checks-stage cost components for each window, ranked by minutes. Include the full-suite `cargo test --locked` demonstration runs in crates/athena-core/src/run/checks.rs (demonstration_runs), and state which component grew between the windows. Cite only jobs from the after window as evidence of the rise, and name the job ids and the measured minutes. Where a number is an estimate, label it. Part 2 is the smallest change in crates/ that removes the largest component that grew, for example by cutting repeated full-suite demonstration runs, with a test that shows the changed behavior. Acceptance: (a) the note's cause accounts for most of the rise from 0.2 to 0.6, shown by the numbers in the note; (b) every cited job is in the correct window; (c) the code change targets the named cause and not a different one; (d) the existing checks pass; (e) the changelog says only what the diff does.
